title: AI Conversational Interviewing: Transforming Surveys with LLMs as Adaptive Interviewers

paper.authors: Wuttke, Assenmacher, Klamm, Lang, Wuerschinger, Kreuter (LMU Munich / MCML / Mannheim / Oxford / Maryland)
paper.repo_note: Scaffold URLs were PDF line-break fragments of this one URL

dependence.note: The LLM is the interviewer agent ('InterviewGPT') that conducts live multi-turn interviews with human students; all outcomes (response quality, interviewer guideline adherence, participant survey) are human-coded properties of those human-AI conversations.

claim.statement: Five GPT-4-Turbo-led in-depth interviews (Chainlit app, GPT-4 turbo 'version 04/2024', voice-assisted) vs. six human-led interviews with students on an identical political questionnaire yielded comparable response quality on 5-point coder scales (relevance 4.6 vs 4.3, clarity 4.3 vs 3.9, engagement 2.6 vs 3.2, specificity 3.1 vs 3.6), longer answers (52.39 vs 32.81 tokens/answer), higher readability (Flesch 77.66 vs 62.22) and similar guideline-violation counts (72 vs 64 per interview), with the AI failing mainly to ask follow-up questions (88% of such violations) (Table 1, Figure 6).
claim.metric: human double-coded quality ratings (2 research assistants, codebook Appendix G), coded interviewer guideline violations (Appendix H), tokens per answer, Flesch reading ease, post-interview survey scores
claim.original_source: Table 1; Findings section 4 text; Figure 6 (guideline violations); Appendix I

protocol.model_note: app-v1/app.py instantiates ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4-turbo-preview', streaming=False) - an alias that resolved to gpt-4-0125-preview (dead) at the time; the paper's '04/2024' suggests gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09. Discrepancy unresolved.
protocol.model_status: dying 2026-10-23 if gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09; dead 2026-03-26 if gpt-4-0125-preview
protocol.endpoint: OpenAI chat completions via LangChain ChatOpenAI inside a Chainlit app (Fly.io); OpenAI Whisper for speech input and tts-1 for voice output; conversation logging via Literal AI
protocol.prompt_source: app-v1/prompt.md (system role 'InterviewGPT', interviewing guidelines, 14-question questionnaire on politics/democracy); paper Appendix C/D

params.other: multi-turn conversation with a live human; ~22 minutes per interview; voice or text input chosen by respondent

protocol.n_items_note: 5 AI-led interviews x 14 questionnaire items (multi-turn); 6 human-led comparators
protocol.evaluation: Human: two research assistants double-code every interviewer turn (guideline violations) and every response (quality dimensions); post-interview survey (Appendix K); observers log technical issues. Automatic: tokens per response, Flesch reading ease (scripts/quantitative-evaluation-scripts/quantitative-evaluation.ipynb), plots in analysis.R

artifacts.notes: Study pre-registered on OSF Registries (link in paper); raw per-annotator data partly withheld for anonymisation.

blockers: requires live human respondents (university students in a Zoom seminar, informed consent, ethics protocol) - not re-executable as an API-only harness
outcome metrics are human-coded by two research assistants using codebooks
n = 5 AI interviews vs 6 human interviews; no inferential statistics - any re-run is descriptive only
model identity ambiguous (paper '04/2024' vs code alias 'gpt-4-turbo-preview')

budget.assumptions: HYPOTHETICAL simulated-respondent replay only (not the original design): 5 interviews x ~30 interviewer turns x 3 seeds; growing context ~2,500 tokens/turn, ~120 output tokens/turn. The original design (human respondents + human coders) has no API cost model.

judgment.rule: Not judgeable under ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 without human participants. If a simulated-respondent replay is approved, only interviewer-behaviour metrics (guideline-violation rate per interview, share of follow-up-question violations, active-listening behaviour) are comparable, judged by direction (AI violation rate ~ human rate; AI far fewer active-listening violations, far more missed follow-ups).
judgment.notes: Response-quality and survey metrics depend on real respondents and cannot be reproduced with a simulated respondent.

user_checks: Policy question: classify human-in-the-loop interaction studies as 'blocked: human participants' uniformly, or allow an LLM-simulated-respondent replay as a successor design for interviewer-behaviour claims only?
If a replay is allowed, which model string - gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (paper) or the code's alias target gpt-4-0125-preview (dead)?
domain_notes: Survey-methodology study (LaTeCH-CLfL 2025) embedded in a student seminar, English questionnaire on politics/democracy for German students; human interviewers were untrained students, which the authors flag as a limitation. Voice input via Whisper with editable transcripts. The AI's characteristic failure - not asking follow-up questions despite explicit instructions, after succeeding in internal pre-tests - is a prompt/model-version-sensitive behaviour, which is exactly what a successor-model re-run would probe.
